1.sofaString: 110	Pt, *****, is a 14 year old male who is diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who is being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.     Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt, his parents, his older brother, and review of the medical records.   SW spent 30 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, *****, lives with his parents and younger brother in ******, *******.  They reside in a single family house with central air conditioning and well water.  They have a filtration system on the water, and do use it for cooking and drinking. They change the air filter monthly.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have indoor ********** and outdoor German Shepherds (which they *****).           Demographics:  Mother: ****** *******  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  37  Employment:  Self-employed with husband. They run a contracting business doing commercial landscaping.   Phone:  ***-***-**** home; ***-***-**** cell     Father:  ******* *******  DOB:  **/**/****    Age:  50  Employment:  Self-employed with contracting business doing commercial landscaping  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  **** *******, DOB **/**/****, age 22  Does not live at home, but works with dad part-time; Has glaucoma and is on disability  ****** *******, DOB **/**/****, age 17     Support systems:  Parents report that they have adequate support.  They have ample friends and family who are able to assist them if needed.  The paternal grandmother resides nearby and is very actively involved with the family. She will likely be present at the time of transplant.  **** is also actively involved although he does not live at home any longer.  He cannot drive due to glaucoma but is able to see well enough to do basic tasks to help out.    Both parents have a vehicle.  In addition, ****** has a truck. They deny that transportation to and from Gainesville will be a problem.  They deny that travel expenses will be problematic as well.  They report that they have more than adequate income from their business.  Dad disclosed that his partners will continue running the business while they are here with *****, and that they will not experience any loss of income.  However, he states that he will likely return home to work after ***** is stable and doing well.  Mom will remain at bedside, and in the transplant housing with *****.       ***** is covered by Medicaid ********/ ********.  He does not receive disability due to parents' income.  This may assist with displacement housing post-transplant.  The family is interested in fundraising through ****. This information was provided.  They disclosed that they are more interested in fundraising for the future expenses in case ***** loses insurance when he is an adult and needs help paying for medications etc.       ***** will be entering the 9th grade next week.  He states he is nervous about starting high school.  He is a good student. He is not on an IEP or 504 plan.  He hopes to one day become a cardiologist.  He does not plan to participate in any extracurricular activities.  He is not able to participate in sports due to his cardiac limitations.  He states his main ***** is playing video games.     Course of illness:        ***** was diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy at the age of 3 yrs.  He is status post septal myectomy.  He is also status post ICD device.  He is currently being evaluated for heart transplant.        Financial Situation:     Family is financially supported by income from parent's business.  ***** is covered by Medicaid ********/ ********.    Family reports they are able to pay for displacement lodging and travel expenses, but do want to ********* for future expenses in case there is a time when ***** is no longer covered by the Medicaid.     Family History:     Family medical history includes diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, COPD, and breast cancer.  In addition, pt's older brother has glaucoma.         There is no reported mental health history. The family denies any substance abuse history.  There is no reported history of DV or involvement with DCF.  The family denies any history of involvement with law enforcement, arrests, or criminal history.       Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence that have been documented at this time.  ***** reports that he is currently on one medication.  He states he takes this independently and the family verbalizes agreement.  He is compliant with exercise restrictions.  It appears that the family is compliant with keeping appointments.           Assessment and recommendations:     The family appears to have adequate support. They have been aware of the possibility of transplant since ***** was a toddler, and are agreeable with moving forward when it is time.  ***** states he would like to get a transplant so that he can be more active and have fewer limitations.  He states he would like to be able to go out and walk around, or help walk the dogs.
